title: Liquid staging protocol for multi-arm A/B tests with rollback scheduler
author: Asha Kumar
description:
Motivation: Multi-arm experiments and noisy traffic patterns made our rigid canary lanes brittle for long-running A/B tests. Liquid staging introduces flexible staging lanes that dynamically allocate traffic across arms using a safety-aware scheduler and provides deterministic rollback snapshots. This PR implements the protocol, the scheduler, runtime hooks, a console surface, and end-to-end tests.

What it does: Liquid staging creates ephemeral 'lanes' that can absorb shadow traffic, warm KV caches, and run gradual ramping across multiple arms simultaneously. A central rollback scheduler tracks per-lane safety signals (latency, error-rate, key-quality metrics) and computes rollback watermarks; when thresholds are breached a coordinated rollback snapshot is applied to affected lanes. The scheduler also supports holdpoints for manual verification and automatic fallthrough to a fallback variant.

Design notes: Uses a two-phase commit-like staging handshake: (1) recruit: create lane, attach shadow stream, start warmup; (2) flow: start phased traffic allocation with smoothing windows; (3) commit: promote lane, drain older lanes. Rollback snapshots are lightweight meta snapshots (routing + pinned model version + KV-clear flags) to guarantee deterministic reversion. Metrics gating is pluggable via policy DSL (policy.v1) and integrates with existing SLO gates.

Files changed: runtime scheduler, rollout controller, API surface (rollouts.v1), console UX, docs, helm values, and new e2e harness.

Testing: unit tests for scheduling heuristics, integration tests simulating multi-arm traffic bursts, and a staging replay harness used to validate rollback determinism. CI had one flaky integration test (staging_replay_test) which required a retry; subsequent rerun passed.

Migration/compatibility: Backwards compatible with existing canary APIs. New features are opt-in via rolloutStrategy: "liquid". If not set, controllers behave as before.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement scheduler and handshake protocol
- [x] Console view for lanes + manual holdpoints
- [x] e2e tests and replay harness
- [x] Policy DSL integration and docs
- [x] Helm values and backward-compatible defaults

Related: Linear ENG-3247 (multi-arm rollout spec), ENG-3310 (rollback telemetry).

review_comments: Diego Morales (2026-02-19): Overall looks good. Can you clarify how lane-level KV cache eviction is coordinated during rollbacks?

Asha Kumar (2026-02-19): We add a 'kv_clear' flag in the rollback snapshot. The runtime drains inflight requests, applies the snapshot and triggers selective KV eviction for keys marked as transient. Added more comments in scheduler.go.
Priya Nair (2026-02-20): I saw a potential N+1 when listing lanes from the console on large accounts. Suggest adding pagination and lazy fetch.
Asha Kumar (2026-02-20): Added pagination hooks and memoized lane summaries in the console component; performance tests show <50ms extra on 500 lanes.
Jonah Lee (2026-02-22): Integration harness is elegant but I hit flakiness on staging_replay_test on macOS runners. Not a blocker, but please add a retry wrapper and a deterministic seed.
Asha Kumar (2026-02-23): Added deterministic RNG seed and retry wrapper; CI reran and passed.
release_notes: Introduce 'liquid' rollout strategy: multi-arm lanes, dynamic traffic smoothing, holdpoints, and coordinated rollback snapshots. Opt-in via rolloutStrategy="liquid". Includes console lane dashboard and policy DSL integration.
